description: A PHP static analysis tool for finding errors and security vulnerabilities in PHP applications

latest_release.body:
<!-- Release notes generated using configuration in .github/release.yml at 9520421041c4de67379270dc17502544dd808140 -->

## What's Changed
### Features
* Add @psalm-cli-only-instances: code requiring an instance of a class only instantiated from the command line is command-line code by @danog in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/13635
* Honour FORCE_COLOR and share color detection across CLIs by @alies-dev in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/13665
* Exit with code 2 when psalter --dry-run would change files by @alies-dev in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/13666
* Let plugins mark a file's top-level code as CLI-only by @alies-dev in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/13643
### Fixes
* fix(match): analyse a match(true) arm once for all its conditions by @jirkace in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/12842
* Perf: analyse an inherited constructor once per subclass (-5 to -9 % CPU) + fix false positive PropertyNotSetInConstructor by @alies-dev in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/13240
* Fix: method with an unknown parameter class is analysed when its file is analysed again by @alies-dev in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/12547
* fix(control-flow): preserve outer loop exits across switch cases #13620 by @orklah in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/13627
* Fix unused variable detection for references returned by functions by @orklah in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/13623
* Name the compared operator in int range comparison messages (#12109) by @jirkace in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/12762
* fix(templates): resolve a method call on a template bounded by another template by @jirkace in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/13107
* fix(closure): a closure that calls itself through a by-reference use has its own signature there by @jirkace in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/13077
* Fix: analyse a file's namespace-level statements once, not for every subclass that follows into it (mediawiki -33 % CPU) by @alies-dev in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/13592
* Fix: invalid file:// links for paths with spaces and Windows drives by @alies-dev in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/13664
* fix(parser): read built-in constants without their deprecation by @shu-chen-dot-ca in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/13601
* [7.x] Keep taint graph nodes as compact rows: worker results ~600 MB → 170 MB, main peak -1.1 GB by @jarstelfox in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/13536
* Fix: psalter rejects the advertised `--monochrome` option by @alies-dev in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/13669
* Fix: generic @mixin binds static to an earlier mixin declaring the same method by @alies-dev in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/13673
* Fix: psalm-refactor --move and --rename never work by @alies-dev in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/13679
* Fix: --show-info, --report-show-info and --threads misread their values by @alies-dev in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/13680
* Fix: options after a path are ignored, so psalter --dry-run can rewrite files by @alies-dev in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/13678
* Fix: psalter --file, --plugin and --codeowner resolve paths wrongly by @alies-dev in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/13681
* Fix: psalm - (paths from STDIN) and empty path arguments crash by @alies-dev in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/13682
* Fix: a class's own @mixin replaces the mixins inherited from its parent by @alies-dev in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/13687
### Internal changes
* Readable psalter output by @alies-dev in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/13656
* Perf: read a location's compact state without a property table (taint, 1 thread: -1.8 % peak memory) by @alies-dev in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/13674
* Require psalm/psalm-plugin-api 0.4.3 by @alies-dev in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/13683
### Other changes
* feat(callable): report a callable that takes a parameter by reference where it is called with a value by @jirkace in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/

detail.readme:
Psalm

[![Packagist](https://img.shields.io/packagist/v/vimeo/psalm.svg)](https://packagist.org/packages/vimeo/psalm) [![Packagist](https://img.shields.io/packagist/dt/vimeo/psalm.svg)](https://packagist.org/packages/vimeo/psalm) [![Psalm coverage](https://shepherd.dev/github/vimeo/psalm/coverage.svg?)](https://shepherd.dev/github/vimeo/psalm) [![Psalm level](https://shepherd.dev/github/vimeo/psalm/level.svg?)](https://psalm.dev/) Psalm is a static analysis tool for finding errors in PHP applications. [Join the official Psalm news channel](https://t.me/psalmphp) and the Psalm community on [Telegram](https://t.me/psalmphp_community) and [Discord](https://discord.gg/RwH8rEpxt9)! ## Installation To get started, check out the [installation guide](docs/running_psalm/installation.md). ## Live Demo You can play around with Psalm [on its website](https://psalm.dev/). ## Documentation Documentation is available on [Psalm’s website](https://psalm.dev/docs), generated from the [docs](https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/blob/master/docs) folder. ## Support Psalm development You can support Psalm development by requesting a support contract from [Daniil Gentili](https://daniil.it), the only active maintainer of Psalm. Support contracts can cover full integration of Psalm into existing codebases, support for Psalm issues and development of additional Psalm features. See [here »](https://daniil.it) for info, pricing and contact information. ## Interested in contributing? Have a look at [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md). ## Who made this Built by Matt Brown ([@muglug](https://github.com/muglug)). Maintained by Daniil Gentili ([@danog](https://github.com/danog)), Alies Lapatsin ([@alies-dev](https://github.com/alies-dev)) and Orklah ([@orklah](https://github.com/orklah)). Former maintainer: Bruce Weirdan ([@weirdan](https://github.com/weirdan)). The engineering team at [Vimeo](https://github.com/vimeo) have provided a lot encouragement, especially [@nbeliard](https://github.com/nbeliard), [@erunion](https://github.com/erunion) and [@nickyr](https://github.com/nickyr).
